name: Pick-and-transport for e-commerce
summary: AMRs carry totes or accompany associates so walking time drops on multi-zone picks. Works best when Wi-Fi and a basic WMS handshake exist and aisles stay wide enough for collaborative traffic.

name: Fixed-lane carton and pallet moves
summary: AGVs suit stable point-to-point routes (dock to buffer, buffer to pack) when the map rarely changes. Infrastructure and guide paths raise upfront cost but stabilize repetitive volume.

name: Collaborative pick assist
summary: Pick-assist fleets bring work to associates or guide picks in zone. Highest payoff when pick density is high and WMS/WES can allocate work to robots and people together.

name: Flexible transport across 3PL clients
summary: AMRs help 3PLs move totes and cartons when client mix and slotting change. Prefer fleets you can redeploy by zone without rebuilding fixed guides for every new shipper.

name: Pick assist for multi-client fulfillment
summary: Collaborative pick assist supports seasonal 3PL peaks when WMS work allocation can target robots and people by client or wave.

name: Stable dock and buffer lanes in a 3PL
summary: AGVs fit long-lived dock-to-buffer lanes that stay the same across clients. Avoid AGV-only designs if client resets constantly reshape pick paths.

name: Pallet moves for 3PL inbound/outbound
summary: Autonomous pallet movers cut forklift trips on wide-aisle inbound and outbound when payload and aisle rules are clear.

name: Line-side material delivery
summary: AGVs deliver kits and components on repetitive plant routes with predictable timing. Strong when aisles and stops stay stable for years.

name: Dock-to-line pallet moves
summary: Pallet movers handle heavy inbound and WIP pallets where forklifts create congestion or safety risk on known paths.

name: Ad-hoc WIP and buffer transport
summary: AMRs cover less predictable WIP moves between cells when a full AGV guide network is overkill.

name: Wave transport in grocery DCs
summary: AMRs support tote and carton moves around grocery waves when ambient zones change more than freezer tunnels. Confirm cold ratings before freezer-only work.

name: Fixed cold and dock lanes
summary: AGVs suit stable dock and cooler-adjacent lanes with high repetitive volume. Factor hygiene and temperature qualification into vendor selection.

name: Pallet outbound for grocery waves
summary: Pallet movers reduce forklift congestion on grocery outbound when aisles and dock doors support autonomous traffic rules.

name: After-hours office vacuuming
summary: Compact robots cover open carpet and hard floors overnight while staff handle restrooms and detailing. Mapping and obstacle handling matter more than industrial scrub depth.

name: Hospital corridor scrubbing
summary: Large scrubbers cover long hard-floor corridors overnight when mapped no-go zones protect clinical areas. Staff keep isolation rooms and detailing.

name: Clinic and admin floor vacuuming
summary: Compact cleaners fit clinics and admin wings with lighter soil than main hospital corridors.

name: Heavy-soil healthcare support areas
summary: Industrial cleaners target loading docks, service corridors, and other high-soil healthcare support zones—not sterile clinical floors.

name: Distribution center floor scrubbing
summary: Large scrubbers handle wide concrete aisles after shifts when dock soil and dust are the main problem.

name: Heavy warehouse floor cleaning
summary: Industrial cleaners fit dusty, tracked-in, or rugged DC floors where compact office robots fail.

name: Food running in full-service dining
summary: Serving robots reduce runner walk time on clear paths during peak. Staff still plate, sell, and handle exceptions; robots are a capacity layer, not a full front-of-house replacement.

name: Food running in QSR and food halls
summary: Serving robots move trays across shared food-hall or QSR paths when congestion is manageable and staff still handle guest exceptions.

name: Bussing in high-turnover dining
summary: Bussing robots help clear tables in high-turnover halls when paths are open and turnover pressure exceeds staffing.
